front_blocks.md: If a tall pea plant with genotype **TT **is crossed with a short pea plant with genotype **tt**, what would be the **possible genotypes** of the offspring?

back_blocks.md: If a tall pea plant with genotype TT is crossed with a short pea plant with genotype tt, all offspring would be **heterozygous** with the** genotype Tt**. This is because a **T **allele is inherited from the tall parent and a** t** allele is inherited from the short parent.

cards.back_md: If a tall pea plant with genotype TT is crossed with a short pea plant with genotype tt, all offspring would be **heterozygous** with the** genotype Tt**. This is because a **T **allele is inherited from the tall parent and a** t** allele is inherited from the short parent.

front_blocks.md: If a tall pea plant with genotype **Tt **is crossed with another tall pea plant with genotype **Tt**, what would be the **phenotype ratio** of the offspring?

back_blocks.md: If a tall pea plant with genotype Tt** **is crossed with another tall pea plant with genotype Tt, the phenotype ratio of the offspring would be **3: 1** (**3 tall and 1 short**). This is because the cross would result in **1 x TT **(tall), **2 x Tt** (tall) and **1 x tt** (short).

front_blocks.md: Define the term **carrier **in the context of sex-linked traits. (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: A carrier is a **female with one recessive allele for a sex-linked trait** that is masked by a dominant allele. She doesn't have the condition but can pass it on to offspring.

front_blocks.md: What is the probability that a **son** born to a** carrier female** will have **colour blindness? **(**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: The probability that a son born to a carrier female will have colour blindness** **is **50 %**:

|   | X<sup>B</sup> | Y |
|---|---|---|
| X<sup>B</sup> | X<sup>B</sup>X<sup>B</sup> | X<sup>B</sup>Y |
| X<sup>b</sup> | X<sup>B</sup>X<sup>b</sup> | **X**<sup>**b**</sup>**Y** |
For any **son** born from the parents shown, the probability that he will have colour blindness is 50 %.
Note that the vision of the father is irrelevant here, as any son will only inherit the Y chromosome from his father.

front_blocks.md: **True or False? **
The Y chromosome typically carries as many genes as the X chromosome. (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: **False. **
The Y chromosome is much** smaller** and carries** fewer genes than the X **chromosome.
